name: Spot Hearts
description: Spot Hearts is a trick-taking variant where each heart scores its pip value (2 through 10 face value, jack 11, queen 12, king 13, ace 14; queen of spades 25). Players avoid winning tricks containing penalty cards; the game is played to a higher target (e.g. 500) and the lowest score wins.

overview.description: Spot Hearts is a trick-taking variant where each heart scores its pip value (2 through 10 face value, jack 11, queen 12, king 13, ace 14; queen of spades 25). Players avoid winning tricks containing penalty cards; the game is played to a higher target (e.g. 500) and the lowest score wins.

history.origins: Spot Hearts is a scoring variant of Hearts. Hearts first appeared at the end of the nineteenth century and is now popular in various forms in many countries; Spot Hearts keeps the standard American Hearts deal and play but assigns penalty points by each heart's pip value and a higher game target.
timeline: Late 19th century: Hearts first appeared; American version and Spot variant use pip-value penalty scoring for hearts.

setup.players: Four players. Spot Hearts is most commonly played by four; there are no formal partnerships.
setup.deck: A standard 52-card deck is used, with no jokers. All 52 cards are dealt out one at a time so each player receives 13 cards. Spot Hearts uses the same deck as standard Hearts; only the penalty scoring differs (hearts count their pip value, queen of spades 25).
setup.dealing: Deal and play are clockwise. All 52 cards are dealt out one at a time so that each player has 13. After the deal, each player passes three cards face-down (first hand to the left, second to the right, third across, fourth hand no pass; the cycle repeats).

rules.objective: The object is to avoid scoring penalty points. Each heart scores its pip value (2–10 at face value, jack 11, queen 12, king 13, ace 14; queen of spades 25). The game is played to a higher target (e.g. 500); the player with the lowest score when someone reaches or exceeds the target wins.
rules.gameplay: Play follows standard Hearts. The holder of the 2 of clubs leads it to the first trick. Players must follow the suit led if possible; the highest card of the suit led wins the trick. Hearts may not be led until a heart has been played to a previous trick (hearts broken), unless a player holds only hearts. Shooting the moon (taking all penalty cards) reverses the score for that hand. Deal and passing cycle are as in standard Hearts.

synthesis.shortDescription: Hearts variant: spot cards have point values; face cards zero.
